recognize_zh: 血片散布數個細長、兩端尖的鐮刀狀紅血球，並有多個含 Howell-Jolly 小體的紅血球、標靶細胞與多染性大紅血球，是鐮刀型貧血的典型表現。
features: Scattered elongated sickle cells with tapered ends
Numerous Howell-Jolly bodies (single small dark round inclusions) in red cells
Target cells and a few large polychromatophilic red cells
One red cell with multiple coarse basophilic inclusions (possible Pappenheimer bodies) at left
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows anisopoikilocytosis with scattered sickle cells having elongated, pointed ends. Howell-Jolly bodies are frequent, and target cells and polychromatophilic macrocytes are present; one red cell contains multiple coarse basophilic inclusions suggestive of Pappenheimer bodies. A few crenated cells are also seen, and platelets are adequate. Findings are consistent with sickle cell disease with features of hyposplenism.

ddx.vs: HbSC has more target cells and blunt, crystal-bearing poikilocytes with fewer classic sickle cells; HPLC distinguishes them.
Sickle trait smears are essentially normal without sickle cells or Howell-Jolly bodies under standard conditions.
Sickle beta-thalassemia shows marked microcytosis and hypochromia with raised HbA2, whereas these cells are normochromic.
Asplenia explains Howell-Jolly and Pappenheimer bodies and target cells but does not produce sickle cells.
